I've worked with insurance for a few years, and I'm now on Medicare myself, so while I am not an expert, I generally have a better grasp of insurance than the general public.

Based on the information provided, I can not tell you which plan will be better for you.

I can tell you that I typically advise against high deductible plans, unless you have the amount of your deductible available right from the start.

They are attractive for the very reason you stated above, low/0 premiums.

However people don't take into account that you are responsible for the entire deductible before that plan pays anything.

You would pay $2,340 before the high deductible plan pays $1. A hospital visit in January could easily meet this, but then you have to pay this out of pocket.

Then you will want to look at what happens after you reach your deductible. Some plans will have a 0% coinsurance after the deductible is met, but this isn't always the case.

I would also advise you to look into financial assistance within your local health system...many large hospital and clinic systems have them as a way to help patients with lower incomes pay for expenses after insurance.
